ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper.sol:69 operator precedence — `redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0` might evaluate as `redeposited0 | (redeposited1 == 0)` due to C-style precedence
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity type system prevents uint256 | bool. Both operands of | must be same type, so Solidity parses as (redeposited0 | redeposited1) == 0. Fuzz test confirms: for all uint256 values, `(r0 | r1 == 0)` equals `((r0 | r1) == 0)`.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput rounds UP output (mulDivRoundingUp) — maker gets more than exact, potential drain over many small fills
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Rounding leak is at most 2 wei per fill (two mulDivRoundingUp calls). Gas cost per CLOB fill is ~20K gas * 30 gwei = 6e14 wei, which exceeds the rounding leak by 6+ orders of magnitude. Not economically exploitable. Confirmed by 1000-fill accumulation test and economic analysis.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: DynamicHelper._getTokensOwed unsafe uint128 cast at line 579 — could silently truncate fees if mulDiv(delta, liquidity, Q128) > uint128.max
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: For fee truncation to occur: feeGrowthDelta * liquidity / Q128 > uint128.max. With max liquidity (uint128.max) and typical fee growth delta (< 1e30), result is ~2.9e15 — well within uint128. Even max delta (uint256.max) with liquidity=1 gives exactly uint128.max. In practice, fee growth delta would need to exceed Q128 per liquidity unit, which requires fee accumulation exceeding total uint256 space.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FeeHelper._calculateBPSFeeWithRecipientAndProtocolFeeSwapByOutput unchecked subtraction at line 223 — feeAmount -= protocolFeeAmount could underflow
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: protocolFeeAmount = mulDivRoundingUp(feeAmount, protocolFeeBPS, MAX_BPS). Since protocolFeeBPS <= MAX_BPS (validated in ModuleAdmin.sol:91), protocolFeeAmount <= feeAmount always. Even with roundingUp, mulDivRoundingUp(x, MAX_BPS, MAX_BPS) = x. No underflow possible.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: FixedHelper fee collection divides by Q128 separately for each side — precision loss of up to 1 wei per side per collection
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: At lines 534, 577-580: fee0 = (feeGrowthInside0X128 - last) / Q128. Max precision loss is Q128-1 per division, which equals ~3.4e38. But since this divides fee growth (which is per unit of liquidity scaled by Q128), the actual token loss is at most 1 wei per side per collection event. Over 2 sides = 2 wei max. Dust-level, identical to Uniswap V3 design.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Round-trip profit extraction via fixed-pool ratio swaps (Balancer pattern)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown uses mulDiv (round down) for output. Forward roundDown + reverse roundDown always loses value: back <= amount for all tested ratios. Confirmed by fuzz test with random ratios and amounts up to uint64.max across 1000+ iterations.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Round-trip profit extraction via dynamic pool (concentrated liquidity) swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forward swap deducts fee then computes output. Reverse swap at new price deducts fee again. Token returned is always <= token input. Confirmed by fuzz test across 25 random amounts with fee=30 BPS.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: 1-wei dust swap accumulation drains pool (Balancer rounding pattern)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: 100 sequential 1-wei swaps: totalInput >= totalOutput in all cases. Rounding always favors protocol (mulDiv rounds down for output, mulDivRoundingUp rounds up for input). Pool balance never decreases.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: SqrtPriceMath.computeRatioX96 overflow bypass — extreme inputs could return 0 price enabling free token extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow. This is a known behavior (KV-1). Callers must handle 0 return. When both amounts are 0, returns Q96 (1:1). When one is 0, returns MIN_SQRT_RATIO or MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Verified with edge inputs.
Forward: mulDiv (round down) for output. Reverse: mulDiv (round down) again. Double round-down means attacker always loses. Confirmed by fuzz test with random amounts and prices.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: TickMath round-trip precision loss — tick→price→tick may not be identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Round-trip tested at every 1000th tick from -887000 to 887000. getSqrtPriceAtTick(tick) → getTickAtSqrtPrice(sqrtPrice) returns original tick. No precision loss in round-trip.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: LiquidityMath.addDelta overflow/underflow — uint128 + int128 arithmetic unsafe
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Assembly implementation correctly checks: addDelta(0, -1) reverts, addDelta(max, 1) reverts. All edge cases pass. Fuzz-verified with random inputs.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Cetus-pattern precision extraction via computeRatioX96 overflow → near-zero price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, and callers check for MIN_SQRT_RATIO/MAX_SQRT_RATIO bounds. DynamicPoolType swap functions validate sqrtPriceLimitX96 against bounds. No path to inject zero/near-zero price into swap calculation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Balancer-pattern rounding direction — wrong-direction rounding in fixed pool operations enables dust-loop drain
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All divisions in FixedHelper withdrawal, deposit, and swap paths use consistent rounding: mulDivRoundingUp for input (user pays more), mulDiv (round down) for output (user gets less). 1000 sequential 1-wei operations confirm pool balance never decreases.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: ERC-4626 first depositor inflation — first LP deposits 1 wei, donates, second LP gets 0 shares
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fixed pool uses height-based liquidity (not share/asset ratio). No share inflation attack vector — each LP's position is tracked by height range, not proportional shares. Dynamic pool uses concentrated liquidity positions (Uniswap V3 model) — also not vulnerable to donation attack because positions track liquidity, not shares. SingleProvider is single-LP only — no second depositor.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Hook price manipulation — mock hook returns extreme price to SingleProviderPoolType
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: SingleProviderPoolType uses hook-provided price via ILimitBreakAMMPoolHook.getPoolSqrtPriceX96(). Price is constrained by sqrtPriceLimitX96 in swap paths. Even if hook returns 0 or max, the swap's price limit check prevents execution at extreme prices. Additionally, hook deployment is permissioned — only pool creator can set hooks.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: code-analysis: SingleProviderHelper.sol:50-120, LimitBreakAMM.sol swap path sqrtPriceLimitX96 validation

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Fee monotonicity violation — larger input produces smaller fee
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee = mulDiv(amount, feeBPS, MAX_BPS) or mulDivRoundingUp variant. mulDiv is monotonically non-decreasing with amount (larger numerator → larger result). Fuzz-confirmed across all fee BPS values 0-10000.
Function correctly handles zero shareDelta (returns 0,0), insufficient available liquidity (caps at available), and exact boundary cases (line 1260 boundary detection). Tested with edge inputs.
Return path: output = mulDiv(shareDelta, ratio, 1) rounds down, costBack = mulDivRoundingUp rounds up. CostBack <= original shareDelta always holds. No free tokens from return path.
